text.p: Moody's Investors Service said it had downgraded Winterthur Swiss Insurance Co's insurance financial strength rating to Aa2 from Aaa.
It also downgraded its ratings on the guaranteed senior unsecured debt of Winterthur Finance Ltd to Aa3 from Aaa.
More than $600 million of debt securities is affected.

"These ratings actions reflect the weakened capital structure of the Winterthur Group, the quality of its earnings, as well as the expectation that that the recently librealised Swiss and German insurance markets, and the company's keener focus on shareholder returns, will result in an increased long-term risk profile," it said in a statement.
Winterthur, Switzerland's largest insurer, has traditionally reported comparatively strong profitability, it added, noting management aims to improve operating efficiency and competitiveness.

Although Winterthur has avoided or withdrawn from riskier classes of business, management has decided to strengthen the company's position through mergers and acquisitions, some of them large, it said.

"The levels of aggregate debt and investment in subsidiaries have therefore increased, whereas the capital resources generated by the Winterthur Group have been fully consumed by goodwill write-offs, dividend payouts and the effects of foreign exchange losses," Moody's said.
"As a result, both the operating and financial leverage of the group have been steadily rising," it said.
It said Winterthur's integration process in Europe, the existing dividend payout and increased pressure on rates in Switzerland and Germany could help weaken its capital structure.

It said the ratings differential between Winterthur Finance's debt, which is guaranteed by the parent, and the parent's strength rating reflected the preferential treatment of policyholders in Switzerland in case of liquidation.
